clue.text: FT pair with urge chopped up tree

indicators.note: something chopped up is cut into bits, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Instructions for a woodcutting pair, told to chop up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' turns the letters of FT, PAIR and URGE into the answer; 'with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit grows on a small evergreen of the same name, so the word names the plant too.

clue.text: Pragmatism is shown in study

indicators.note: the word is is displayed inside another word, so these words signal a container

parts.note: a realm is a field or domain of study

explanation.surface: A philosophy student finds pragmatism discussed in a study.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a practical outlook that accepts things as they are rather than as one might wish.

clue.text: Current value found by Dirac for one quantum expert

indicators.note: one piece is placed beside the other, so this signals putting them side by side

parts.note: Paul Dirac, the British physicist
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A physics paper reports a value of current that Dirac found.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolfgang Pauli, of the exclusion principle, was a quantum physicist like Dirac.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang Pauli was a founding figure of quantum mechanics, an example of such a specialist.

clue.text: See 24
To ensnare nobleman he returned in new guise, secretly and illegally

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap something inside, so one piece goes within the other
a new guise is a fresh disguise, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A man comes back in disguise to trap an aristocrat, acting covertly and outside the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's disguised returner is the anagram: 'in new guise' shuffles the two words to UNDERTHEER, and 'To ensnare' traps the nobleman within. The phrase recalls goods sold out of sight beneath a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes goods sold or deals done covertly, away from proper legal sale.

clue.text: Try to catch start of hockey or bit of cricket?

indicators.note: to catch is to hold something within, so a container

parts.note: to tax is to try or strain someone, as in taxing patience

indicators.note: the start of the word hockey is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sports question asks about catching in hockey or a part of a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket here is the insect, not the bat-and-ball game the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's body has a middle segment carrying the legs and wings, so it is part of a cricket insect.

clue.text: Italian's here — an unknown quantity to test

parts.note: qui is the Italian word for here
z is an algebraic symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: An Italian points to an unknown quantity and sets a test.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to question someone in order to check what they know.

clue.text: Still silent about embarrassing display? Not entirely

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: silent means quiet

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a scene is a public fuss or embarrassing show

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent about an embarrassing episode, though not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' opens the clue looking like an adverb; it is the definition. 'Not entirely' clips the fuss to SCEN before 'about' wraps the silence round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something at rest, inactive or dormant, with no movement.

clue.text: Really cool Liverpudlian's first to stop diamonds hoax

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: cod means a hoax or sham, British slang

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word Liverpudlian's

explanation.surface: A cool Liverpudlian puts a stop to a hoax involving diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated phrase means extremely chilled, literally very low in temperature.

clue.text: Footballer about to be dropped by United or City

indicators.note: to be dropped is to be left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a back is a defensive footballer
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A footballer is about to be dropped by Manchester United or City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is not 'nearly' but C (circa); 'United or City' look like football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan, so an example of a city.

clue.text: Editors aim to produce publication

indicators.note: producing here means making something new from the words, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Editors set out to produce a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: RADIO TIMES is a long-running British magazine of television and radio listings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a weekly British listings magazine, an example of a periodical.

clue.text: Swimmer stays popular in defeat

indicators.note: stays here means holds or supports, so one piece keeps the other inside

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A swimmer stays popular despite losing a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish an opponent off is to beat them completely, so the verb works as a synonym.

clue.text: Spooner's exhibited line for live broadcast

indicators.note: Spooner swapped opening sounds of words, so the first sounds are exchanged

parts.note: showed means exhibited
a row is a line

explanation.surface: An exhibition line for a live programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of SHOWED ROW gives ROAD SHOW by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring programme broadcast from a different place each time, often live.

clue.text: Flower from husband after angry words with a mum

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another in the answer

parts.note: ma is a mother, mum
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A flower comes after a husband has angry words with his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant with tassel-like crimson blooms, known as love-lies-bleeding, is an example of a bloom.

clue.text: Having mental aberration, bowled out in bad weather

indicators.note: out means removed, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden mental disturbance
b is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricketer has a mental lapse and is bowled out in poor weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm bringing heavy rainfall is a clear case of foul conditions.

clue.text: Work companion right to leave cheesy town

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Cheddar is a Somerset village famous for its cheese
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A colleague goes off to a famous cheese town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'companion' is CH (Companion of Honour), not a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a medieval Icelandic collection of mythological poetry, an example of a literary piece.

clue.text: All there is in college poetry?

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether college poetry holds everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos is everything that exists, matching the phrase exactly.

clue.text: I'd use light weapon and have Jack die horribly

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters of the word die are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fighter boasts of a light weapon that will make Jack die horribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars knights wield lightsabers, so one could say this of themselves.

clue.text: Porno books in Heather's collection?

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: erica is the botanical name for heather
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Pornographic books turn up in Heather's collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms name sexually explicit material, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Very consistent cricket umpire

definitions.meaning: David ... was an English Test match cricket umpire

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire known for very consistent decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means unvarying; the other is the surname of a well-known English umpire.

clue.text: New German individual holds king in cell

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: neu is German for new
one means a single individual
R, for rex, is king

explanation.surface: A new German individual holds a king in a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell transmitting signals; this is a variant spelling of the usual term.

clue.text: Sleep with caprine deity in vessel offered by tender

parts.note: to bed someone is to sleep with them
Pan is the goat-legged Greek god

explanation.surface: A seduction aboard a boat with a goat god.
explanation.walkthrough: The tender is a nurse, not a small boat as 'vessel' suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle a nurse brings to bedridden patients for toilet use.

clue.text: Regret very much hearing influential thinker

indicators.note: hearing means we go by how the words are spoken

parts.note: rue means regret, and so means very much

explanation.surface: Someone deeply regrets hearing a thinker's ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was an Enlightenment philosopher whose ideas shaped modern politics.

clue.text: Go to Frenchman for Parisian in mist

parts.note: va is French for go
pour is French for for

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a Frenchman for a Parisian in the fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine moisture suspended in the air, the same as a haze or steam.

clue.text: Old bike makes little girl more distant object

parts.note: Penny is a short form of the girl's name Penelope
far as in the far side, the more distant of two
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: An old bike makes a little girl a distant figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A PENNY-FARTHING is a Victorian bicycle with a huge front and tiny back wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian high-wheeled bicycle is named after two coins of unequal size.

clue.text: NT promisee annoyed with me?

indicators.note: annoyed means stirred up, so the letters of the words NT and promisee are mixed

explanation.surface: A New Testament figure given a promise is annoyed with the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In the gospels Jesus promised Peter the keys of heaven, yet also rebuked him: 'Get thee behind me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle given the promise of the keys in Matthew, and the one Jesus rebuked.

clue.text: Approval withheld in retreat?

parts.note: withheld means refused, a no
OK means approval

explanation.surface: Approval refused, a person heads off to a quiet corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded corner where one can withdraw from others, a hideaway.

clue.text: Miles with friend offers hand

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Miles and a friend offer a helping hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner surface of the hand, used to stand for the whole hand.

clue.text: North Surrey rowing team — they're active at Kew

indicators.note: rowing is read as quarrelling, upset, so letters are rearranged

parts.note: a team's players are its men

explanation.surface: A rowing crew from north Surrey trains on the Thames near Kew.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW Gardens is London's botanical garden, beside the Thames near Surrey; 'rowing' means arguing.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who raise plants for sale are the sort found at a botanical garden.
